skeleton: plump, friendly Spinosaurus walking on all fours, three-quarter view turned to the left, its head up at the front on a thick neck: root on the ground under the body; body (pivot over the legs) with belly squash, the body piece carrying the cream throat and the neck up under the head (its top a soft unoutlined edge) and its back running into the root of the tail, ending in a soft unoutlined cut the tail tucks under; sail (the tall rounded striped sail, one piece behind the body, its base hidden behind the back) on the belly; head (no neck, soft unoutlined bottom) on top of the neck, face with eyes (the far one smaller, by the snout), brows and mouth; four legs at the shoulders and hips, each whole to the webbed foot: legFF (far front, behind the chest) and legBF (far back, under the tummy), shaded; legFN and legBN (near, in front of the body); foldFN/foldBN (none at rest) swap in for the near legs folded under when it lies down; the long paddle tail behind the body, its bone at the join.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a plump, friendly blue-green Spinosaurus with darker teal spots, a cream throat and tummy, a tall rounded sail on its back with soft orange-and-yellow stripes and spots, a long paddle-shaped tail and big webbed feet, walking on all fours, turned a little to the left. Draw this exact Spinosaurus as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body with its neck: the plump, rounded blue-green body with its darker teal spots and its cream throat and tummy, turned as in image 1, without head, without sail, without legs and without tail: the back one smooth outlined curve with no sail on it, no legs, shoulders, thighs or feet drawn on it, the cream underside one smooth round shape. At the front, the cream throat and the spotted blue-green back of the neck go up and forward from the shoulders, as wide as the neck is under the head in image 1, keeping the curved line of the back of the neck as in image 1, and end in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the head). At the back, the spotted back runs on smoothly into the very root of the tail and ends there in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no round bump, no stump, no line where the tail would join.
2. the sail alone: the tall rounded sail with its soft scalloped top edge, its orange and yellow stripes fanning out and its little spots, exactly as in image 1, drawn whole including the part normally hidden behind the back; its bottom a soft straight band of orange with NO outline along the bottom (it is hidden behind the back).
3. the head alone, without neck: the head with its short rounded snout, its two little nostrils, the darker teal spots on top and the rosy cheek, turned as in image 1, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth and no mouth line, the snout and the cream jaw one smooth shape; keep the nostrils, the spots, the rosy cheek and the little bumps of the head's outline where the eyes sit. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head, round the snout and along the jaw under the snout to the chin, as in image 1. From the chin round to the back of the head its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the cream throat and the blue-green back of the head simply stop there, about level with the bottom of the rosy cheek.
4. the tail: the long, flat, paddle-shaped spotted tail with its cream underside, as in image 1, drawn whole from its thick root (normally hidden inside the body) to its rounded paddle tip pointing to the right; its root a soft, smooth edge cut straight across with NO outline.
5. the far front leg: the leg on the far left of image 1, behind the cream chest, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden behind the chest) down to its big webbed foot with its soft rounded toes, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
6. the near front leg: the front leg in the middle-left of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden inside the body) down to its big webbed foot with its soft rounded toes, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
7. the far back leg: the leg partly hidden under the tummy between the near legs in image 1, drawn whole from the top of its thigh (normally hidden behind the tummy) down to its webbed foot with its soft rounded toes; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
8. the near back leg: the big back leg on the right of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its big round thigh down to its big webbed foot with its soft rounded toes, as in image 1, the round thigh with its outline as in image 1.
9. the near front leg as when the Spinosaurus lies down on its tummy: the same leg folded under, seen from the side, its webbed foot tucked forward flat on the ground; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
10. the near back leg as when the Spinosaurus lies down on its tummy: the same big round thigh with its outline, the leg folded flat under it, the webbed foot tucked forward flat on the ground.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no pointed claws, no spikes. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a plump, friendly blue-green Spinosaurus; image 2 shows the same Spinosaurus cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the Spinosaurus's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Spinosaurus in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, just behind the snout) is smaller and narrower than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look to the left and a little up: each big dark-brown iris sits towards the left of its eye, the white on its right, a white sparkle at its upper left.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a tall oval eye, its big dark-brown iris with a white sparkle towards the left, the white on its right, outlined in dark brown.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, a warm-brown iris with a dark pupil and a white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U, with two little lashes.
4. sad: open and round, a soft warm-brown iris with a white sparkle and a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim, looking down and to the left; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, to the left, the iris towards the left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, mouths, none with any teeth: 17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a long, thin, closed smiling line running back along the snout, gently curved, curling up into a little smile at its right end. 18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, under the snout, the inside pink with a little pink tongue, smooth inside, no teeth. 19. the mouth open in a small round 'o', the inside pink. 20. the mouth in a small sad frown. 21. the mouth wide open in a big round yawn, the inside pink with a little tongue, smooth inside, no teeth. 22. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside. 23. the mouth puckered in a little round sniff: a small closed bud of a mouth.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the Spinosaurus waddles along on its four webbed feet, its sail rocking gently and its paddle tail swaying, then stops.
the Spinosaurus swims along to the left, its head and sail above the water and its paddle tail sweeping, then stops.
the Spinosaurus crouches, gives a happy little hop with all four webbed feet off the ground and lands with a soft squash.
the Spinosaurus nods its head yes, twice.
the Spinosaurus shakes its head no.
the Spinosaurus looks one way, then the other, then back.
the Spinosaurus laughs and laughs, its round tummy bouncing with giggles.
the Spinosaurus does a happy little dance, stepping from foot to foot, swaying its sail and swinging its paddle tail.
the Spinosaurus talks, its mouth moving, its head bobbing a little.
the Spinosaurus cries, head down, little tears falling, its tummy shaking with sobs.

pause.shows: the Spinosaurus crying, head down, eyes squeezed shut with tears

animations.description: the Spinosaurus gives a big yawn, lies down on its tummy with its legs tucked under it and falls asleep, then wakes up, gets up and smiles.

pause.shows: the Spinosaurus lying on its tummy fast asleep, eyes shut, head resting low

animations.description: the Spinosaurus shivers and trembles, cold or scared.
the Spinosaurus lifts its paddle tail and slaps it down, splash, then does it again and giggles.
the Spinosaurus sweeps its long paddle tail up and down, slow and strong, like a paddle.
the Spinosaurus lifts its chin and stretches its big sail up to the sun, eyes closed happily, warm and cosy, then relaxes.

pause.shows: the Spinosaurus basking, chin up and sail stretched up tall to the sun, eyes closed happily

animations.description: the Spinosaurus lowers its snout and sniffs, sniff, sniff, then lifts its head with a happy smile.

pause.shows: the Spinosaurus with its snout down, sniffing

animations.description: the Spinosaurus shakes the water off its body, wiggle, wiggle, from its head to its paddle tail, then smiles.
